searchText: Ok, I found the issue Prysm validator accounts do not accept the chain config flag So, there is no way to generate valid deposit signatures without hacking prysm deep to the core ``` [2020-05-20 10:24:48] ERROR main: flag provided but not defined: -chain-config-file ``` Am I correct that `0x00000113` is `[0, 0, 1, 19]` ? https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/5922 I will hack the mainnet config to get valid deposits And hopefully we can address this in Prysm My teku node won't start. 😢 https://github.com/PegaSysEng/teku/issues/1813 Witti is already off to a difficult start 😜 > ^C^C^C^C^C^C^C^C^C^C^C^C^C^C > ^C It seems like you had trouble stopping it 😛 😄 Do invalid deposits count towards min validator count? It looks like my Prysm node is already working towards a genesis whereas Lighthouse still waits for deposits. > Do invalid deposits count towards min validator count? <@!557201004060213248> according to spec they aren't (only active validators) Ok, lighthouse seems to count the deposits regardless of validity. https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/issues/1178 Prysm already announced a genesis event in 20 minutes, so I suspect they might accept invalid accounts. Will know more at 10am UTC So the deposit is part of the total deposit count whethere they are valid or not it is still part of the deposit tree yes but the minimum deposit count should only contain valid deposits right? because you cannot launch a chain with invalid deposits correct , the min genesis validator count needs valid deposits I guess we can also start logging the 'active count' to give a better idea of the current genesis validator count that is probably more useful than the total deposit count AFAIK we won’t trigger genesis with invalid validators The count we show usually is the gross deposit count It’s not cheap to calculate the valid deposit count “minimum deposit count met” doesn’t mean we count the invalid deposits towards genesis. It just means that we transition to the stage where we start checking validity. There’s another log (potentially debug) that shows the active validator count, which takes into account validity Yes, the ticket above is just of cosmetic nature So, Prysm started the chain but Lighthouse didn't Different genesis times ? <@!476250636548308992> it looks like you do indeed count invalid deposits because I don't know why it would launch already What is the minGenesisCount ? and how many deposits did you send 96 128 96 is min genesis count how many of the 128 are invalid ? 32 but I just did the last deposits a couple of minutes ago, it shouldn't be visible in prysm Am i missing something ? shouldn't it start then there is a min follow distance of 1024 right? the valid deposits should not be visible thats not in the spec yet afaik its supposed to come in v0.12 Has Prysm actually started, or does it just know the genesis time? it started proposing blocks yes and lighthouse didn't even see the deposits yet <@!476250636548308992> https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/v0.11.3/configs/mainnet.yaml#L41 So AFAIK the spec isn’t clear as to wether we follow genesis deposits at the follow distance or not (not at PC, can’t verify) The spec has the genesis delay set such that it doesn’t matter the spec doesn't define the follow distance for genesis deposits But if the genesis delay is less than the follow distance then there’s an issue ok so which client is correct then? IMO we should follow at the distance. It’s there to protect against reorgs, why shouldn’t that count at genesis too? If we don’t follow genesis at the same follow distance as voting then we get this odd jump in time too, potentially invalidating some deposits the spec defines it only using the genesis delay, not the follow distance ```py genesis_time=eth1_timestamp - eth1_timestamp % MIN_GENESIS_DELAY + 2 * MIN_GENESIS_DELAY, ``` if we follow the spec to the word the genesis time doesn't take into account for the follow distance Does the spec define where you’re getting the eth1 blocks from? I’d say that it’s undefined and unclear either way this should be specified on how we determine ``` eth1_timestamp ``` yeap agreed that should be clarified Agreed I can create a discussion if you like I had assumed that this was the case, I should have flagged it at the time. I didn’t actually notice my assumption. ``` eth1_timestamp is the Unix timestamp corresponding to eth1_block_hash ``` this should probably be changed Given that we should follow deposits at follow distance, I think a configuration that sets the delay to be less than the follow distance is bound to result in skipped slots. Would need to do some more thinking to come up with a concrete statement about this, though. https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/issues/1832 You can probably keep the chain running as is for now, we’ll just rock up a bit late Fashionably late 😛 No, I rather pull the launch Don’t drink all the beers before we get there, Prysm! Teku is stuck and Prysm requires a couple of hacks We still have to do some work I think we need to set `genesis delay >= follow_distance` for now sounds good > I think we need to set `genesis delay >= follow_distance` for now <@!476250636548308992> I want to be able to create testnets without waiting a day. So I would rather be in favor of defining the eth1 timestamp to honor the delay Also, if you could take a look at https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/5922 please? 🙏 That makes sense , ok will look at this today fwiw, nimbus synced to the broken schlesi block and rejected whatever it got from the peer it was connecting to: ``` NOT 2020-05-20 12:39:02+02:00 Block: root verification failed tid=705819 file=state_transition.nim:92 block_state_root=d8ec43fc state_root=d2e0f469 NOT 2020-05-20 12:39:02+02:00 Invalid block topics="clearblk" tid=705819 file=clearance.nim:179 blck="(slot: 150496, proposer_index: 24, parent_root: \"ecbcbfa7\", state_root: \"d8ec43fc\", proposer_slashings_len: 0, attester_slashings_len: 0, attestations_len: 2, deposits_len: 0, voluntary_exits_len: 0)" blockRoot=813d4fd9 cat=filtering pcs=block_addition ``` It looks like you guys have the correct state root :) ,afaik that is the same state root as the pyspec maybe lots of clients isn't a bad idea after all 😉 😄 It's certainly unsafe to make decisions on eth1 blocks before the follow distance. Due to that, the genesis delay should probably just always be greater than the follow distance for safety. There are a number of unwritten relationship between some of the configs and this is certainly one of them. I'll write it that this relationship should hold, otherwise, genesis is likely to be missed at the start. > fwiw, nimbus synced to the broken schlesi block and rejected whatever it got from the peer it was connecting to: > <@!449019668296892420> Can you share me some multiaddreses I can sync from? 🙂 <@!557201004060213248> to have quick chainstarts you probably can set the eth1 follow distance as a much smaller amount. Ex: ``` 16 ``` as long as the ``` genesis_delay > eth1_follow_distance * time_per_eth1_block ``` I wouldn't wave this away that easily, we see different behavior in different clients and even though I can adjust the variables it should still be addressed yes, agreed. Will make clear the correct behaviour in the spec right now
